title: Mammalian Cell Division in 3D Matrices via Quantitative Confocal Reflection Microscopy
protocol: Plate HEK 293T cells on a 10 cm cell culture dish at the density of 5 x 10^6 cells per dish in DMEM containing high glucose, sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS, and 1% Pen/Strep.
Incubate for 24 h at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Ensure that the confluency of HEK 293T cells is about 70 - 80% on the day of transfection.
Transfect HEK 293T cells using a transfection reagent with three plasmids.
Mix 6 µg of H2B-mCherry plasmid, 8 µg of CMV ΔR 8.91, and 2 µg of pMDG-VSVG in 1 mL of reduced serum media.
Incubate the DNA mixture at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Add 48 µL of transfection reagent to the DNA solution.
Incubate the DNA-lipid complex at room temperature for at least 15 minutes.
Carefully add the DNA-lipid complex solution drop-wise to the cells.
Gently swirl the plate to ensure even distribution of the complex.
Aspirate the medium approximately 6 hours after transfection.
Add fresh cell culture medium (DMEM with high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS, and 1% Pen/Strep).
Harvest the supernatant at 24, 48, and 72 hours post-transfection.
Replace the medium after each harvest with DMEM containing high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS, and 1% Pen/Strep.
Filter the lentiviral particles through a 0.45 µm filter to remove cellular debris.
Alternatively, spin down the supernatant to separate out cell debris.
Store the supernatant at -80 °C or use it for transduction immediately.
Plate MDA-MB-231 cells at a density of 1 x 10^5 cells in a 35 mm culture dish.
Add 1 mL of virus and 1 mL of fresh medium (DMEM with high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS, and 1% Pen/Strep) to the cells 24 hours after plating.
Incubate the cells for a period of 6 hours to overnight.
Plate MDA-MB-231 cells at 50 to 60% confluency in each well of a 24-well plate.
Incubate the culture at 37 °C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Replace growth medium with 0.5 ml medium containing 2 mM thymidine.
Leave in incubator for 24 h.
Release the cells from thymidine exposure by washing them with phosphate buffered saline (PBS) three times.
Incubate cells in normal cell culture medium (DMEM, high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS and 1% Pen/Strep) for 5 h.
Block the cells with 250 ng/mL of nocodazole for 12 h.
Shake the cells for 45 s to 1 min using an orbital shaker at 150 to 200 rpm.
Remove the medium to extract cells by pipetting the medium into a centrifuge tube.
Add 0.5 mL of fresh medium (DMEM, high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS, and 1% Pen/Strep) to each well of the plate.
Repeat steps for shaking and removing medium three times.
Centrifuge the collected medium containing the mitotic cells at 800 x g for 3 min.
Aspirate the medium from cells collected in step 2.9.
Re-suspend cells in about 0.25 - 0.5 mL of fresh cell culture medium (DMEM, high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS, and 1% Pen/Strep).
Place 10 µL of the re-suspended cell solution on a hemocytometer and count the density of the cells in the solution.
Determine the volumes needed for all components to make the 3D collagen matrix.
Calculate the volume of the cell solution needed to obtain 40,000 cells/mL (or 20,000 cells for the 500 µL of collagen gel).
Calculate the volume of 10x DMEM needed: 50 µL.
Calculate the volume of FBS needed: 50 µL.
Calculate the volume of collagen I stock needed based on a concentration of around 4 µg/µL.
Calculate the volume of sodium hydroxide needed to neutralize the acetic acid in the collagen solution.
Determine the volume of the filler solution: (500 µL total gel - X µL cells - 50 µL 10X DMEM - 50 µL FBS - Y µL collagen - Z µL NaOH) = R µL
If the calculated volume is negative, re-suspend cells in a smaller volume of medium.
Add cells in medium to a clean 1.5 mL centrifuge tube on ice.
Pipette 10X DMEM into the tube on ice.
Add FBS to the tube on ice.
Add deionized (DI) water as filler solution to the tube on ice.
Add collagen to the tube on ice.
Add NaOH to the tube on ice.
Mix the solution carefully with a 1 mL pipette after adding NaOH.
Transfer 500 µL of the mixed solution to each well of a 24-well plate.
Place the 24-well plate in a 37 °C incubator.
Prepare fresh cell culture medium in a 37 °C water bath.
Add 500 µL of pre-warmed medium (DMEM, high glucose (4.5 g/L), sodium pyruvate, 10% FBS and 1% Pen/Strep) to the top of the gel 30 min after completing step 3.7.
Turn on the live cell unit mounted on top of the objective lens.
Wait until the temperature stabilizes at 37 °C, the concentration of CO2 is at 5%, and the humidity is at 75%.
Put the 24-well plate of gels into the live cell unit on the microscope.
Find the bottom of the plate and then move the objective lens up until the microscope focuses at about 500 µm from the bottom of the plate.
Move the stage around to find the cells, and select multiple positions for imaging.
Set up the time-lapse experiment at 2-min intervals.
Turn on the live cell unit mounted on top of the objective lens.
Wait until the temperature stabilizes at 37 °C.
Ensure the concentration of CO2 is at 5%.
Ensure the humidity is at 75%.
Configure a confocal microscope to capture only reflected light (488-nm) from the 488-nm laser used to illuminate the sample.
Use a 60X water-immersion objective with NA = 1.2 and WD = 200 µm for imaging.
Put the sample (cells in collagen matrices) into the live cell unit.
Find the bottom of the plate.
Move the objective lens up until it focuses at about 100 µm from the bottom of the plate.
Select multiple positions for imaging.
Set up the time-lapse experiment at 5 min intervals.
Use Z-stack to collect images from successive slices at 5 μm intervals, spanning a total of 25 μm.
Quantify the deformation of the collagen matrix in the vicinity of a cell using particle imaging velocimetry (PIV) with sub-pixel resolution.
Apply anisotropic low pass filtering to enhance the signal of the collagen network.
Extract a regional window of 15×15 pixels centered at (x,y) from frame k.
Identify the best matching locations (x,y)* through maximum normalized cross-correlation coefficient in the image obtained at frame k+1.
Calculate the deformation vector as (x,y)* - (x,y).
